entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Ottoman Empire's invasion of Malta in 1565, known as the Siege of Malta, was a pivotal event in European history. 

 The siege began on May 28, 1565, when the Ottoman forces, led by Grand Vizier Mehmed Sakıp Paşa, arrived in the Grand Harbour of Malta. The defenders, led by Grand Master Jean Parisot de Valette, held out for 112 days, despite being outnumbered and outgunned. The siege ended on September 18, 1565, with the defeat of the Ottoman forces. 

 The Siege of Malta marked a turning point in the history of Malta, as it secured the island's independence from the Ottoman Empire and cemented its position as a strategic location in the Mediterranean. 

 The siege has become a symbol of the island's resilience and bravery, with the phrase 'Ein fawwara' (We still have water) being used to describe the defenders' determination.
